semantics: libical: icalrecur_iterator_new(rrule, dtstart) then icalrecur_iterator_next() until it returns a null time. The iterator yields only instances generated by the rule: a DTSTART that does not match the rule is NOT emitted (include_dtstart=false; e.g. the WKST=FR BYWEEKNO case). All values are copied verbatim: floating local DATE-TIME, UTC (Z) or DATE; no time zones (TZID) are involved, and UNTIL is compared against the floating/UTC value as written. Every rule has COUNT or UNTIL (or is expected to be rejected), so 'expected' is the complete instance list (no limit). The upstream harness additionally (a) iterates backwards with icalrecur_iterator_prev() and expects the reversed list, and (b) for cases without START-AT and without SKIP, re-runs the case once per expected instance using that instance as DTSTART with COUNT reduced by its index, expecting the remaining tail. For START-AT cases the harness calls icalrecur_iterator_set_start(START-AT) (forward; expects the instances >= START-AT) and icalrecur_iterator_set_range(START-AT, DTSTART) (backward; expects instances <= START-AT); here 'expected' is always the full list from DTSTART and the START-AT value is given in 'comment'. error=true means icalrecur_iterator_new() is expected to fail ('*** UNIMPLEMENTED' in the source). icalrecur_test_rscale.txt is the expectation for a libical build WITHOUT ICU; icalrecur_test_rscale_withicu*.txt for a build WITH ICU (the dangi file additionally needs ICU's Dangi calendar). RSCALE/SKIP are RFC 7529 and marked in 'extensions'.
